title: Cold rebuild: A key ring
summary: Rebuild A key ring from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A key ring** in *Key management and storing secrets*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Before retiring v1, you count which key each stored value uses. What does this print?
steps.explain: Two values still need v1, so v1 cannot be destroyed yet. The key id in front of every value is what makes this question answerable at all.

steps.title: Rebuild A key ring cold
prompt: Write two methods over a key ring `Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys` (key id to 32-byte AES key):
- `string Encrypt(Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys, string currentId, byte[] nonce, string text)` returns `"<currentId>:<Base64 of nonce + ciphertext + tag>"` using AES-GCM.

- `string Decrypt(Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys, string token)` reads the id before the **first** `:`, looks the key up, and decrypts. An unknown id throws `KeyNotFoundException` (the dictionary indexer does that for you).
The tests encrypt with `v1`, rotate to `v2`, and check both still decrypt.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
string Encrypt(Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys, string currentId, byte[] nonce, string text)
string Decrypt(Dictionary<string, byte[]> keys, string token)
